predecessors.note: New Spain: 'At its conclusion in 1821, the viceroyalty was dissolved' (Spanish Empire dossier). Cliopatria's Spanish Empire shape still holds Mexico in 1820-1821 and its First Mexican Empire row begins in 1822.

successors.note: 1 July 1823, after the empire's end in March.

union.text: New Spain's lands north of Central America: the Mexican heartland and the northern borderlands, without the Captaincy General of Guatemala

correction.text: New Spain's borders 'from northern California' to the Mexican south (the page's infobox territory list names California, Texas, New Mexico, Utah, Nevada and Arizona), before the Captaincy General of Guatemala joined

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the empire exists from Mexican independence (27 September 1821) but Cliopatria's row begins in 1822. The page says its territory 'corresponded to the borders of' New Spain, so in 1821 the Central American provinces are not yet in. Same northern correction as the 1822 shape (California, Nevada, Utah, Arizona). The infobox's 4.43 M km2 (1821) is the page's figure for the whole territory 'corresponded to the borders of' New Spain; this shape, the Mexican part without Central America, is smaller by design.

correction.text: the Cliopatria shape plus California, Nevada, Utah and Arizona, which the page lists in the empire's territory ('stretch[ed] from northern California' to Central America)

keyframe_review.note: 3.63 M km2 against the infobox 4.43 M km2 for 1821 (ratio 0.82, inside the factor of two). The shape holds Mexico, Texas, New Mexico and all five Central American countries but only a sliver of California (0.06) and of Arizona (0.28) and none of Nevada or Utah, while the page says the empire stretched 'from northern California' to Central America and lists California, Nevada, Utah and Arizona; so the four are added. The page excludes Panama (then in Colombia), as the shape does. Colorado and Wyoming are left as Cliopatria has them.

region.text: New Spain's lands north of Central America: the Mexican heartland and the northern borderlands, without the Captaincy General of Guatemala

ledger.note: 1821: Mexico declares independence and the empire begins. Independence 27 September 1821 (infobox); the Plan of Iguala of 24 February 1821 is the infobox's 'Established' date and the Treaty of Cordoba followed (24 August 1821 in the text, September 1821 elsewhere on the page). The territory 'corresponded to the borders of' New Spain; the page gives the viceroyalty, not a boundary.

region.text: Chiapas, then part of the Captaincy General of Guatemala

ledger.note: 1822: Chiapas is inside the empire. The page is silent on when Chiapas joined; it says only that Chiapas was 'the only province that remained part of Mexico' after the Central American federation formed. Cliopatria's 1822 shape includes it.

region.text: the Captaincy General of Guatemala's provinces, independent since 15 September 1821

ledger.note: 1822: the Central American provinces join the Mexican Empire. 'The junta voted for annexation on 5 January 1822.' The First Mexican Empire page: the provinces 'joined the Empire shortly after their independence'.

1822: the provisional government becomes a monarchy. Infobox government 'Provisional government (1821-1822); unitary constitutional monarchy (1822-1823)'; '21 July 1822 was set as the date of the official coronation' of Agustin I. The page gives no date for his proclamation.

region.text: the empire's Mexican lands, passed to the Provisional Government of Mexico; Central America leaves on 1 July 1823

ledger.note: 1823: Agustin I abdicates on 19 March and the empire ends. Infobox 'Abdication of Agustin I: 19 March 1823'; on 26 March Iturbide agreed to leave the capital and power passed to the Provisional Government of Mexico, which 'abolished the monarchy and established the First Mexican Republic'.

region.text: the Central American provinces, without Chiapas

ledger.note: 1823: Central America leaves Mexico. 'The congress declared Central American independence from Mexico on 1 July' 1823, 'except for the state of Chiapas'; General Filisola had called the new congress on 29 March.

wars.name: Plan of Casa Mata revolt
wars.outcome: The army of Veracruz pledged to restore Congress; Iturbide reconvened it on 4 March, abdicated on 19 March 1823, and the empire gave way to the provisional government.
wars.note: 'On 1 February 1823 a junta in Veracruz proclaimed the Plan of Casa Mata.' No territory changed hands in the fighting; the page does not describe any campaign.

certainty.note: The page describes the territory as the borders of New Spain and gives no boundary line; the northern frontier and the limit of the Central American provinces are approximate throughout.

notes: Cliopatria has only 1822-1823 for the empire; the page dates it from independence (27 September 1821), so a 1821 keyframe is added. The Spanish Empire dossier already records the 1821-09 loss of New Spain to first-mexican-empire and the 1821-09 loss of Central America to 'Central America (Act of Independence)'; this dossier uses the same counterpart string for the January 1822 gain. The page lists California, Nevada, Utah and Arizona in the empire's territory while Cliopatria draws only slivers of California and Arizona and nothing of Nevada or Utah: both keyframes add them (Alta California, Nevada and Utah then stay in the Mexican shapes until the 1848 cession; see federated-republic-of-mexico). The page does not date the proclamation of Agustin I (19 May 1822 is not on it) or Chiapas joining; Chiapas is recorded at confidence 1. The page contradicts itself on the Treaty of Cordoba (24 August vs September 1821). Soconusco is not on either page. The Soconusco page (opened for the federated-republic-of-mexico dossier) says Chiapas was divided in 1823 and that 'Mexico annexed Chiapas formally in 1824'; that dossier records the formal annexation as a 1824 gain, so Chiapas is Mexican here from 1822 only on the Empire page's word (confidence 1).
